events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I’ll inspect the project structure and existing stack, then build the book list, add form, detail pages, and JSON-file persistence within those conventions.

args.content:
# Margin

A small reading journal with a currently-reading shelf, a finished shelf, book notes, and individual book links. No accounts or database.

## Run locally

```sh
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Set `PORT` to use a different port. `npm run dev` starts the same server. Run `npm test` for API and persistence checks, and `npm run build` for syntax checks.

Books are stored in `data/books.json`. The server writes changes to that file, so keep the file on a persistent, writable filesystem. Book links use `/books/<id>` and work on direct load and after a server restart. To share links with other people, host the app at a reachable URL; a localhost link is only reachable on your own machine.

There is no authentication: anyone who can reach the app can see and change its library. Don't put private notes in a publicly accessible instance.

events.content:
Built a small reading journal with currently-reading and finished shelves, an add-book form, notes, and a direct link for each book. Books are saved in data/books.json and remain there after a restart.

Run npm start, then open http://localhost:3000. To send someone a book link, the app needs to be hosted at an address they can reach.

Verification: npm test passed (2/2, exit 0); npm run build passed (exit 0). The running server returned HTTP 200 for the app, its assets, and the books API. No browser-based visual check was run.

There are no accounts, so anyone who can reach the app can view and change the library.
